title: An AI that explains why the market moves. Free early access
author: Character-Truth1991
selftext:
Built this over the past year, solo. Tapewise, a market and news scanner with an AI analyst on top. The pitch in one line, every trading app shows you what moved, mine explains why it moved.

How it works: the scanner reads the news and the tape all day and flags what matters, and the AI turns it into plain English. You open it in the morning and you're briefed, what happened overnight, what's driving today. A headline breaks and it names which tickers it hits and in what way, including the knock on effects (an oil supply cut means refiners catch a bid while airlines get squeezed, that kind of chain). Click any mover and you get the reason behind the move. There's also a journal that fills itself from broker screenshots and finds where you keep losing money.

What it deliberately doesn't do: buy or sell calls. It explains, you decide. Partly compliance, partly just what I wanted to build.

It's at [tapewise.io](http://tapewise.io), free during early access, everything unlocked

comments.author: Capital-Field3324
comments.body:
Interesting, however am quite skeptical of the ai analyst. An LLM will give you an answer for any question you throw at it. What perturbs is whether the answer is correct or hallucinated ?

Do not know what framework you have under the hood(ai analyst) to avoid hallucinations?

I suppose know what happened yesterday could prove beneficial mainly in capitalising on long term spill over effects.Where by news or price moves in some stocks affect related stocks either negatively or positively

replies.author: Character-Truth1991
replies.body:
You're right to be skeptical tbh, an LLM on its own will confidently answer anything. The way we handle it is to never let it answer from memory. Every request gets the actual data stuffed into it (live price, volume, the day's headlines for that exact ticker, the economic calendar) and the instructions are basically if the reason isn't in this data, say you don't see one. So instead of inventing a catalyst it will literally output "no clear news behind this one, looks like it's just moving with its sector". 

Few other things, news from social sources arrives pre labelled as unconfirmed and it has to say so. It knows its own training cutoff and today's date, so anything that could have changed since (mergers, IPOs, whatever) has to come from the live feed or it tells you to go check a proper source. And it's not allowed to do predictions or price targets at all, it only explains what's already happening, so there's way less room to be confidently wrong about the future.

Is it hallucination proof? nothing is. But giving it the real data at answer time and making "I don't see a reason" an acceptable answer gets you most of the way there. And the spill over thing you mentioned is honestly the main feature, when news drops it maps who else feels it (suppliers, competitors, the second order names nobody's watching). That's the part an LLM is good at.
